name: Barbell Jefferson Curl
resistance_profile: Loads the erectors eccentrically through full segmental spinal flexion; tension is highest at the fully rounded, deeply stretched bottom position.
cues: Keep the bar light — this is a slow control lift, not a strength test
Roll down one vertebra at a time, chin tucked first
Restack from the bottom up: hips, low back, mid back, head last
execution_steps: Stand on a sturdy box or bench high enough for the bar to travel below your feet, holding an empty or lightly loaded barbell with an overhand, shoulder-width grip; feet together, knees straight but not locked.
Tuck your chin, then roll down one vertebra at a time — upper back, mid back, low back — letting the bar slide down the front of your legs.
Go only as deep as you can control: stop at a full but comfortable stretch, and never bounce at the bottom.
Reverse it slowly, restacking the spine from the bottom up until you are standing tall, with your head coming up last.
good_when: You want to train the erectors through a full flexion range to build tissue tolerance
You have healthy spinal range of motion and want a slow, controlled mobility-strength movement
bad_when: You have an acute disc injury or pain with loaded spinal flexion
You can't move the bar slowly and with control — this is a light, deliberate lift, not a heavy one
common_errors: Loading it like a deadlift and losing segmental control
Bouncing at the bottom instead of owning the stretch
Hinging only at the hips rather than flexing the spine
progressions: Add small plates (1.25–2.5 kg) once a slow, segmental rep feels easy
Increase range by standing on a taller box
regressions: A dowel or an unloaded bar
Reduce range with a partial roll-down to mid-shin
